premises: Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, delaying crack initiation.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) can be induced in tungsten-based refractory HEAs via controlled thermal treatments.
SCCPs provide both precipitation hardening and progressive strain hardening, enhancing strength and ductility simultaneously.
The SCCPs design concept yields ~1 GPa yield strength at 800 °C and ~15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature in a tungsten HEA.
The proposed mechanism and property improvements are achievable under spark plasma sintering with optimized cooling rates.
